model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for six different model configurations, including a baseline “Vanilla” model and several variants of “StrmLLM” and “SepLLM” with varying parameters such as batch size (n=64 or n=128) and architectural modifications (H, H/T). The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 in linear scale with major gridlines and tick labels every 20,000 iterations. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 in linear scale, with major tick marks and gridlines at intervals of 0.1. All lines begin near a loss of 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep initial decline, followed by a slower, steady decrease toward convergence. The “Vanilla” model (purple solid line) starts highest and remains slightly above others throughout. “StrmLLM (n=64)” (teal solid line) drops quickly and stabilizes around 2.65 by 140,000 iterations. “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange solid line) follows closely, ending slightly lower. “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green solid line) and “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red solid line) show nearly identical trajectories, both converging near 2.55. The “SepLLM (n=128)” model (dark blue solid line) starts slightly lower than “Vanilla” and converges to approximately 2.52, making it the lowest-loss model at the final iteration. All lines are smooth and solid, with no markers, indicating continuous training loss tracking.
